5	\label{sec:exp-setup}
6	
7	We evaluate SICA against Self-Consistency (SC) across six models, three reasoning domains, and over 3,000 condition-evaluations (${\sim}$1,250 unique instances), with diagnostic analyses of confirmation bias and process-level independence (\S\ref{sec:analysis}).
8	
9	\paragraph{Models.} Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen3-14B (non-thinking mode)~\citep{yang2024qwen25}, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3~\citep{jiang2023mistral}, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct~\citep{dubey2024llama3}, and QwQ-32B~\citep{qwen2024qwq} (7B--32B). We additionally evaluate SCB universality via cross-model extraction on five frontier models (gpt-4o, gpt-4.1, gpt-5.5, o3, Gemini-2.5-Pro; Table~\ref{tab:frontier-scb}), where Mistral-7B extracts constraints from the target model's traces since closed-source APIs do not expose internals suitable for self-extraction.
10	
11	\paragraph{Datasets.} FOLIO~\citep{han2022folio} ($n{=}204$, with gold logical annotations), ProofWriter depth-5~\citep{tafjord2021proofwriter} ($n{=}600$), LogiQA~\citep{liu2020logiqa} ($n{=}200$). StrategyQA~\citep{geva2021strategyqa} ($n{=}200$) serves as a domain-formalizability diagnostic. GSM8K~\citep{cobbe2021gsm8k} ($n{=}30$) and AIME 2024 ($n{=}22$) probe the degenerate regime ($C_0 < 5\%$).
12	
13	\paragraph{Parameters.} $K{=}12$ traces at $T{=}0.7$, extraction at $T_{\text{ext}}{=}0.3$, $\alpha{=}0.5$, Z3 timeout 10s. McNemar exact test ($\alpha{=}0.05$); 95\% bootstrap CIs ($10{,}000$ resamples) for $n \geq 200$. SICA incurs $4.5{\times}$ SC wall-clock; extraction accounts for 76\% of overhead.

1	\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
2	
3	Test-time computation scaling through multiple reasoning samples has emerged as a practical alternative to scaling model parameters \citep{snell2025scaling, guo2025deepseekr1}.
4	The dominant aggregation strategy, Self-Consistency (SC) \citep{wang2023sc}, samples $K$ chain-of-thought traces and selects the majority answer.
5	SC is simple, model-agnostic, and effective---but it is hitting a ceiling.
6	\citet{loo2025reevaluating} demonstrate that gains from increasing $K$ plateau and even decline for strong models.
7	The gap between SC's theoretical promise (independent correct voters converge to truth) and its practical behavior (saturating gains) points to a structural mismatch: same-model traces carry correlated errors, and majority voting has no mechanism to correct shared bias.
8	
9	Confidence-weighted \citep{taubenfeld2025cisc} and universal \citep{chen2024usc} extensions alleviate this, but the core limitation persists.
10	Recent neuro-symbolic methods \citep{pan2023logiclm, olausson2023linc, xu2026dylos, li2025aristotle, wang2025fover, luo2025logicagent} report gains on logical reasoning but introduce components beyond the reasoning model.
11	A simpler question precedes these: can the \emph{same} model extract useful formal constraints from its own traces---a zero-cost upgrade requiring no additional model or data?
12	No prior work has systematically evaluated this.
13

tool_args.new_string: \looseness=-1 Open-source models range from 7B to 32B parameters with self-extraction; frontier models confirm SCB universality but use cross-model extraction via Mistral-7B, as closed-source APIs do not expose internals---whether self-extraction on frontier models would yield different BR values remains untested. All datasets are English-language logical reasoning benchmarks; we do not evaluate trained symbolic extractors, multilingual settings, or commonsense domains lacking gold annotations. McNemar power is below 21\% for $|\Delta| = 2$\,pp at $n{=}200$--$600$, meaning small true effects may go undetected; most conditions use a single seed (four-seed $\Delta$ range spans ${\sim}4$\,pp). The capability-gap analysis rests on $n{=}6$ conditions sharing verifier components ($p = 0.167$ after collapsing); we characterize it as a consistent pattern rather than a confirmed law. SICA requires $4.5\times$ the wall-clock time of SC with no significant accuracy gain. Extended limitations are discussed in Appendix~\ref{app:limitations-extended}.

\paragraph{Why it works.}
\looseness=-1 Three conditions jointly enable the escape: (i)~\emph{structural independence}---encoder-only DeBERTa and decoder-only Mistral share no architecture or training data (\S\ref{sec:mirage}); (ii)~\emph{positive capability gap}---verifier standalone accuracy exceeds generator SC (Finding~2); (iii)~\emph{task-verifier alignment}---NLI classification naturally matches premise-conclusion structure. Per-label complementarity: NLI excels on \textsc{False} (71.43\% vs.\ 38.10\%), SC dominates \textsc{Unknown} (68.12\% vs.\ 18.84\%). All three NLI architectures produce significant gains at $w \geq 3$ (Appendix~\ref{app:multi-nli}).

tool_args.old_string:
\paragraph{Disagreement-Routed Cascade.}
\looseness=-1 Full SC+NLI ensemble invokes NLI on every question, but high-agreement questions gain little from external verification. \textbf{Disagreement-Routed Cascade (DRC)} invokes DeBERTa-large-mnli only when the fraction of $K$ traces voting for the majority answer falls below threshold $\tau$; above $\tau$, SC majority vote is used directly. DRC at $\tau{=}0.7$ recovers 90\% of full-combo gain on ProofWriter ($+6.00$ out of $+6.67$\,pp) at 38.8\% NLI cost, and 83.3\% on held-out FOLIO ($+2.45$ out of $+2.94$\,pp) at 34.8\% cost (Table~\ref{tab:drc}, Appendix). A sensitivity sweep over $\tau \in \{0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9\}$ shows the gain concentrates on weak generators: only Mistral-7B (SC $< 40\%$) benefits across all thresholds; stronger models show no DRC improvement, consistent with the capability gap hypothesis.
tool_args.new_string:
\paragraph{Disagreement-Routed Cascade.}
\looseness=-1 \textbf{DRC} invokes NLI only when the fraction of $K$ traces voting for the majority answer falls below threshold $\tau$; above $\tau$, SC is used directly. At $\tau{=}0.7$, DRC recovers 90\% of full-combo gain on ProofWriter ($+6.00$/$+6.67$\,pp) at 38.8\% NLI cost, and 83.3\% on FOLIO ($+2.45$/$+2.94$\,pp) at 34.8\% cost (Table~\ref{tab:drc}, Appendix). A $\tau$ sweep confirms the gain concentrates on weak generators (SC $< 40\%$), consistent with the capability gap hypothesis.

\paragraph{Main result.}
\looseness=-1 DeBERTa NLI alone achieves 49.51\% on FOLIO (below SC's 55.88\%) and 55.00\% on ProofWriter (above SC's 39.33\%). On FOLIO ($n = 204$), combo mode yields $+0.49$\,pp at $w{=}1$ and $+2.94$\,pp at $w{=}3$ (both n.s.). On ProofWriter ($n = 600$), $w{=}3$ achieves $+6.67$\,pp ($p < 0.001$) and $w{=}5$ reaches $+11.00$\,pp ($p < 0.001$)---while same-model SICA \emph{degrades} ProofWriter ($-2.83$\,pp, raw $p = 0.014$; BH adj.\ $p = 0.112$; Table~\ref{tab:main_results}), illustrating that corrective signal must originate outside the model's distribution (\S\ref{sec:mirage}). We report $w{=}3$ as primary. After BH correction ($m{=}12$), Mistral-7B $w{=}3$ (adj.\ $p = 6.78 \times 10^{-5}$) and $w{=}5$ (adj.\ $p = 7.41 \times 10^{-6}$) remain significant; all other conditions are non-significant.

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patheffects as pe
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.patches import Patch

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'DejaVu Sans',
    'font.size': 6,
    'axes.labelsize': 7,
    'xtick.labelsize': 6,
    'ytick.labelsize': 5.5,
    'figure.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.bbox': 'tight',
    'savefig.pad_inches': 0.02,
    'axes.spines.top': False,
    'axes.spines.right': False,
    'pdf.fonttype': 42,
    'ps.fonttype': 42,
})

raw_data = {
    "Prompt-Level": [
        ("Contrastive prompting", -1.1),
        ("Cross-model (Q14B→M)", -0.98),
        ("Cross-model (w→s)", 0.0),
        ("Z3 feedback", 0.0),
        ("Cross-trace UNSAT", 0.0),
        ("Multi-temperature", 0.0),
        ("Discrim. filtering", 0.0),
        ("Generational", 0.49),
        ("Cross-model (Q3→M)", 0.98),
    ],
    "Method-Level": [
        ("LLM-Debate", -18.63),
        ("Contrastive Scoring", -9.31),
        ("ICG", -0.49),
    ],
    "Additional": [
        ("MIN-UNSAT", -6.5),
        ("PROVE (code verif.)", -1.9),
        ("Prob. perturbation", -1.0),
        ("Cross-model SICA", -0.49),
        ("Z3 trace filter", -0.49),
        ("CEGIS (iterative)", 0.0),
        ("DeepConf (logprob)", 0.0),
        ("κ-aware SC", 0.0),
        ("Bootstrapped gold", 0.0),
        ("Sel. abstention", 0.0),
        ("ASCII perturbation", 0.0),
    ],
}

COLORS = {
    "Prompt-Level": '#56B4E9',
    "Method-Level": '#E69F00',
    "Additional": '#009E73',
}

CLIP_X = -12.0
ROW_STEP = 0.55
GROUP_GAP = 0.35

for cat in raw_data:
    raw_data[cat] = sorted(raw_data[cat], key=lambda x: x[1])

categories_order = ["Prompt-Level", "Method-Level", "Additional"]

names, values, colors, y_positions = [], [], [], []
cat_boundaries = []

y = 0
for gi, cat in enumerate(categories_order):
    if gi > 0:
        y += GROUP_GAP
    y_start = y
    for name, val in raw_data[cat]:
        names.append(name)
        values.append(val)
        colors.append(COLORS[cat])
        y_positions.append(y)
        y += ROW_STEP
    cat_boundaries.append((y_start, y - ROW_STEP, cat))

y_positions = np.array(y_positions)

display_values = []
is_clipped = []
for v in values:
    if v < CLIP_X:
        display_values.append(CLIP_X)
        is_clipped.append(True)
    else:
        display_values.append(v)
        is_clipped.append(False)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.3, 3.3))

ax.axvspan(-1, 1, alpha=0.06, color='#888888', zorder=0)
ax.axvline(x=0, color='black', linewidth=0.5, zorder=2)

for gi, (y_start, y_end, cat) in enumerate(cat_boundaries):
    if gi > 0:
        sep_y = y_start - GROUP_GAP / 2
        ax.axhline(y=sep_y, color='#cccccc', linewidth=0.4, zorder=1)

bars = ax.barh(y_positions, display_values, height=0.36, color=colors, alpha=0.85,
               edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.2, zorder=3)

for i, (clipped, val) in enumerate(zip(is_clipped, values)):
    if clipped:
        bx = CLIP_X
        by = y_positions[i]
        zz_x = [bx + 0.06, bx - 0.09, bx + 0.09, bx - 0.06]
        zz_y = [by - 0.12, by - 0.04, by + 0.04, by + 0.12]
        ax.plot(zz_x, zz_y, color='white', linewidth=1.2, zorder=5,
                solid_capstyle='round')
        t = ax.text(bx + 0.15, by, f' {val:.1f}pp ←',
                    ha='left', va='center', fontsize=4.5, fontweight='bold',
                    color='#b37400')
        t.set_path_effects([pe.withStroke(linewidth=1.5, foreground='white')])

for i, (val, dv) in enumerate(zip(values, display_values)):
    if is_clipped[i]:
        continue
    if abs(val) < 0.01:
        continue
    if val <= -5:
        ax.text(dv / 2, y_positions[i], f'{val:.1f}', ha='center', va='center',
                fontsize=4.5, color='white', fontweight='bold')
    elif val < -1.2:
        ax.text(dv - 0.12, y_positions[i], f'{val:.1f}', ha='right', va='center',
                fontsize=4.5, color='#555555')
    elif val > 0:
        ax.text(dv + 0.12, y_positions[i], f'+{val:.2g}', ha='left', va='center',
                fontsize=4.5, color='#555555')

ax.set_yticks(y_positions)
ax.set_yticklabels(names)
ax.set_xlabel('Δ (pp) vs. Self-Consistency')
ax.set_xlim(-13.5, 2.2)
ax.set_ylim(y_positions[-1] + 0.45, y_positions[0] - 0.45)

ax.grid(axis='x', alpha=0.12, zorder=0)
ax.spines['left'].set_visible(False)
ax.tick_params(axis='y', length=0, pad=2)

legend_elements = [
    Patch(facecolor=COLORS["Prompt-Level"], alpha=0.85, label='Prompt-Level (9)'),
    Patch(facecolor=COLORS["Method-Level"], alpha=0.85, label='Method-Level (3)'),
    Patch(facecolor=COLORS["Additional"], alpha=0.85, label='Additional (11)'),
]
ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='lower left', fontsize=5,
          framealpha=0.92, edgecolor='#dddddd', handlelength=0.8,
          handletextpad=0.3, borderpad=0.3, labelspacing=0.25)

ax.text(0, y_positions[0] - 0.38, '±1pp', ha='center', va='top',
        fontsize=4.5, color='#aaaaaa', fontstyle='italic')

plt.tight_layout(pad=0.2)

outdir = '/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0513_3/projects/symb_invariant_consensus/figures/paper'
plt.savefig(f'{outdir}/fig2_interventions_compact.pdf')
plt.savefig(f'{outdir}/fig2_interventions_compact.png', dpi=300)
plt.close()
print('Done: fig2_interventions_compact.pdf')

## 叙事整合要求

### 核心论点：Regime-Dependent Bottleneck
不要笼统说 "extractor dominates" 或 "generator dominates"。正确表述：
- ProofWriter（合成推理，约束 well-defined）→ extractor 是主导因子
- FOLIO（自然语言推理，约束更模糊）→ generator 是主导因子
- **统一结论**：cross-model extraction 在两种 regime 下都无法可靠逃逸 SCB

### Extractor Confound (R12-EC1) 回应
在 §6 或 Limitations 中明确写：
- FOLIO 上 cross-extractor McNemar 不显著 (p=0.143) / 仅 marginal (p=0.021, 6/204 题)
- 因此单 Mistral extractor 的 confound 在 FOLIO 上影响有限
- ProofWriter 上 extractor 确实主导，但这恰好支撑 "regime-dependent" 发现

### SCB 跨数据集普遍性
BR>1 在全部 8 个 cell（2 datasets × 4 combinations）中成立 (range 1.94-2.70)。写入 §5.2 作为 SCB universality 的额外证据。

### Process-κ Pattern 复现
FOLIO 2×2 复现 Process-κ 核心 pattern：低 κ generator (Mistral 0.46) 受益于 cross-ext (+3.92pp)，高 κ generator (Qwen3 0.79) 不受益 (-1.47pp)。在 §6 capability-gap 段引用。

On Mistral-7B FOLIO, when SICA errs, 83.3\% of constraints support the incorrect answer---bias ratio $4.97\times$ (Table~\ref{tab:cross-model-bias})---and 94\% of errors overlap with SC. A shuffle control reveals this bias is \emph{structural}: randomizing constraint--answer associations while preserving per-trace counts yields $\text{BR}_\text{null} \approx \text{BR}_\text{obs}$ ($p > 0.7$), indicating that BR reflects the trace-count distribution rather than extraction-specific error. Z3 rejects only 3.4\% of constraints, and MAX-SAT produces answers identical to count-only aggregation on 94.4\% of problems (Table~\ref{tab:ablation}), confirming that the formal verification layer is vacuous (Eq.~\ref{eq:degenerate}): 99\% of constraints pass Z3 validation yet add no information beyond majority voting.
